title: bOPEN Skills Registry and Tenant Activation Architecture
executiveSummary: Implement the registry as a bounded modular-monolith module, preserve immutable skill versions, and separate publication, tenant entitlement, enablement, agent binding, and per-tool authorization.

principles: A skill is a procedure and not a permission.
Every tool call is independently authorized in validated active tenant context.
Published skill versions are immutable and digest-bound.

decisions.title: Registry topology
decisions.context: P0 needs governed skill metadata without a separate operational service.
decisions.decision: Implement the registry as a bounded module in the bOPEN modular monolith.

alternatives.name: Separate microservice
alternatives.reason: No independent scaling or ownership evidence yet

consequences: The module must expose owned contracts and avoid direct cross-module table access.

controls.requirement: Tenant context is server validated and missing context fails closed.
Skill selection never grants tool authority.
Tenant-owned registry rows use PostgreSQL RLS with default deny.

risks.mitigation: Canonical ID, source authority, explicit override

unresolvedItems: Select registry signing service after technology freeze.
